topic: Strange borders countdown: Brazil-Uruguay twin towns to India's enclaves
hook: Your shopping street in Brazil ends in Uruguay, and nobody stops you crossing it.
title: Your Street Ends in Another Country: 6 Odd Borders
description:
Six real borders that look like map mistakes, from a Brazilian street that runs into Uruguay to the enclaves India and Bangladesh finally swapped in 2015. Each one is stranger than the last, and every one can be checked on a map. Tell us which border you would live on.

#borders #geography #mapfacts
comment_prompt: Which border would you live on?

chapters.title: 6: Brazil and Uruguay Share a Street
5: The US Town Cut Off by Canada

scenes.narration: Your shopping street in Brazil ends in Uruguay, and nobody stops you crossing it.
scenes.headline: Brazil Meets Uruguay

scenes.narration: Today I have six real borders that make no sense, and every single one is stranger than the one before it.
scenes.headline: 6 Borders, All Real

scenes.narration: By the end, you will see a place in India where land sat inside land, inside other land, inside another country.
scenes.headline: India's Is Last

scenes.narration: Some of these borders run through parks. Some cut off whole towns. One of them was never even drawn on the water.
scenes.headline: Parks, Towns, Water

scenes.narration: You can find every one of them on a map, and you can check each fact yourself after the video.
scenes.headline: Check Them Yourself

scenes.narration: Stay till the end, because number one is in India, and it involves tiny plots of land stacked inside each other.
scenes.headline: Number One Is Indian

scenes.narration: We start at number six, where the border is a park and the two towns share the same pavement.
scenes.headline: Starting At Six

scenes.narration: Number six. Santana do Livramento in Brazil and Rivera in Uruguay look like one single town from above.
scenes.headline: One Town, Two Countries

scenes.narration: But you are looking at two countries, and the line between them is very hard to spot on the ground.
scenes.headline: Spot The Border

scenes.narration: In many places, a row of small border markers is all that separates Brazil from Uruguay.
scenes.headline: Just Border Markers

scenes.narration: In other places, a long public park sits right on the line, so you can walk across it without noticing.
scenes.headline: A Park Is The Border

scenes.narration: Walk along one pavement, and you can pass from Brazil into Uruguay between one shop and the next.
scenes.headline: Shop To Shop, Country To Country

scenes.narration: In Brazil, people speak Portuguese. A few steps away in Uruguay, the main language is Spanish.
scenes.headline: Two Languages

scenes.narration: Many locals speak a mix of both, so one single conversation can slide across the border and back.
scenes.headline: A Mixed Language

scenes.narration: Rivera has duty-free shops, so many Brazilian shoppers happily walk across the line just to buy things there.
scenes.headline: Cross To Shop

scenes.narration: A special agreement between the two countries lets people in border cities like these work, study and use public services on both sides.
scenes.headline: Work On Both Sides

scenes.narration: So a person can live in one country and go to school or work in the other, every single day.
scenes.headline: Live In One, Work In Other

scenes.narration: Imagine paying for your chai in one country and walking home to another before it even cools.
scenes.headline: Chai In Two Countries

scenes.narration: Two flags, two languages, two countries, and one shared pavement. That is number six.
scenes.headline: One Shared Pavement

scenes.narration: But a border that is easy to cross is only the start. Next, an American town that cannot reach America.
scenes.headline: Next: A Cut-Off Town

scenes.narration: Number five is a piece of the United States that you cannot reach by road without leaving the United States.
scenes.headline: A Cut-Off US Town

scenes.narration: Number five. Look at the map near Vancouver, and you will find a piece of the United States hanging off Canada.
scenes.headline: Point Roberts

scenes.narration: It is called Point Roberts, in Washington state, and it sits on a small peninsula just below the forty-ninth parallel.
scenes.headline: A Tiny Peninsula

scenes.narration: The border between the US and Canada follows that line of latitude, so this little tip ended up on the American side.
scenes.headline: A Straight Line On Paper

scenes.narration: The problem is that the rest of America is a long way off, across water and across Canada.
scenes.headline: Far From Home

scenes.narration: To reach the rest of the United States by road, a resident has to drive into Canada first.
scenes.headline: Drive Through Canada

scenes.narration: That means crossing a border to go to the American mainland, and crossing another border again to come back home.
scenes.headline: Two Crossings, Same Trip

scenes.narration: Minnesota has a similar oddity called the Northwest Angle, a piece of land you can only reach by land through Canada.
scenes.headline: Northwest Angle Too

scenes.narration: On a map, these places look like mistakes. They are what you get when treaty makers draw straight lines across land they barely mapped.
scenes.headline: Lines Drawn In Haste

scenes.narration: A straight line on paper, and a town that needs a border crossing to go home. That is number five.
scenes.headline: Number Five Done

scenes.narration: Number four is an entire town that sits inside another country, and it has been there for hundreds of years.
scenes.headline: Four Is Centuries Old

scenes.narration: Number four. Llívia is a Spanish town sitting completely inside France, with French land on every side.
scenes.headline: Spain Inside France

scenes.narration: The story goes back to 1659, when Spain and France signed the Treaty of the Pyrenees after a long war.
scenes.headline: The Treaty Of 1659

scenes.narration: France was given a set of villages in this area. But Llívia was officially a town, not a village.
scenes.headline: Village Or Town?

scenes.narration: Because of that wording, Llívia stayed Spanish, and the French villages around it went to France.
scenes.headline: One Word Decided It

scenes.narration: One word in a treaty left a Spanish town stranded, with a different country in every direction.
scenes.headline: Stranded By A Word

scenes.narration: Today, a short road links Llívia to the rest of Spain. It is called the neutral road.
scenes.headline: The Neutral Road

scenes.narration: The road crosses French land, but it is kept neutral so that people can travel between the town and Spain.
scenes.headline: Spain Through France

scenes.narration: Visitors come to Llívia for its old pharmacy museum and mountain views, and the border is just a quiet road.
scenes.headline: A Quiet Border Town

scenes.narration: If you like strange places and facts like these, subscribe, because there is another one waiting tomorrow.
scenes.headline: Like Strange Places?

scenes.narration: So far, every border has been odd. But number three is a German town that lives inside Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Odder Still

scenes.narration: Number three. Büsingen am Hochrhein is a German town of old houses, a church and a river, surrounded by Switzerland.
scenes.headline: Germany Inside Switzerland

scenes.narration: Büsingen is part of Germany. Its people are German citizens and follow German law.
scenes.headline: Legally German

scenes.narration: But the town sits inside the Swiss customs area, so businesses there are treated like part of Switzerland.
scenes.headline: A Swiss Customs Zone

scenes.narration: Both euros and Swiss francs are used in town, even though Germany only uses the euro.
scenes.headline: Two Currencies

scenes.narration: Even the car number plates are special. They start with BÜS, so you can spot a Büsingen car on the road.
scenes.headline: Plates Start BÜS

scenes.narration: From the outside, Büsingen looks like a quiet village on the Rhine. All of the strangeness is hidden in the map.
scenes.headline: Quiet On Top

scenes.narration: A German town in Switzerland, with its own plates and two currencies. That is number three.
scenes.headline: Number Three Done

scenes.narration: Number two is even stranger, because this border does not exist at all. And it is on the water.
scenes.headline: A Border You Cannot Find

scenes.narration: Number two. Lake Constance, where Germany, Switzerland and Austria meet, has no agreed border across its water.
scenes.headline: Lake Constance

scenes.narration: On land, borders are clear. But on this big lake, the three countries never signed a line through the middle.
scenes.headline: No Line On The Water

scenes.narration: The three countries have different views on how to divide the water, and they have never agreed on one answer.
scenes.headline: Three Different Views

scenes.narration: So when a boat sails across the middle of the lake, there is no official line to tell you which country it is in.
scenes.headline: Which Country Is This?

scenes.narration: Ferries, fishermen and sailors share the water through practical agreements instead, so daily life carries on without any trouble.
scenes.headline: Life Goes On

scenes.narration: A famous lake with three countries on its shore, and not one official line anywhere on its water. That is number two.
scenes.headline: Number Two Done

scenes.narration: Now for number one, and it is right here in India, which is exactly why I saved it for last.
scenes.headline: Now: India's Border

scenes.narration: Number one. On the border between India and Bangladesh, in West Bengal's Cooch Behar region, the map once looked like a puzzle.
scenes.headline: A Border Like A Puzzle

scenes.narration: Small patches of India sat inside Bangladesh. And small patches of Bangladesh sat inside India.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: In India, we know these patches as chhitmahals, the word used for these enclaves along the Bengal border.
scenes.headline: Called Chhitmahals

scenes.narration: Some were just villages, with farms, houses and families cut off from the country they belonged to.
scenes.headline: Cut Off From Home

scenes.narration: Then it got stranger. One plot was an Indian piece of land inside a Bangladeshi piece inside an Indian piece inside Bangladesh.
scenes.headline: Land Inside Land Inside Land

scenes.narration: It was called Dahala Khagrabari, and it was the only one of its kind in the whole world.
scenes.headline: Dahala Khagrabari

scenes.narration: People in such pockets often struggled to get a school, a hospital or electricity, because the country around them did not own them.
scenes.headline: No School, No Hospital

scenes.narration: For years they lived in the middle of a country that was not theirs, and their own government could not easily reach them.
scenes.headline: Living In Limbo

scenes.narration: Then in 2015, India and Bangladesh swapped these lands. One hundred and eleven Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh, and fifty-one Bangladeshi ones came to India.
scenes.headline: The Great Swap, 2015

scenes.narration: People living there got a choice of which country to belong to, and families had to decide where their future would be.
scenes.headline: A Choice Of Country

scenes.narration: It was a rare border clean-up on this scale, and it happened right here in South Asia.
scenes.headline: A Rare Clean-Up
scenes.visual_query: Narendra Modi Sheikh Hasina land boundary

scenes.narration: So one of the strangest borders in the world was in our own backyard. Now it is a puzzle that has been solved.
scenes.headline: India's Strangest Border

scenes.narration: That was all six: a shared street, a stranded American town, a Spanish town in France, a German town in Switzerland, a lake with no line, and India's puzzle map.
scenes.headline: All Six Borders

scenes.narration: So go back to the start: your shopping street in Brazil really does end in Uruguay, and nobody stops you crossing it.
scenes.headline: Brazil To Uruguay

scenes.narration: Next video: another place that sounds fake but is completely real. Same channel, same strange maps.
scenes.headline: Next: Another Real Place
